learningObjective: Diagnose KV cache OOM under long-context multi-tenant serving and identify effective mitigations.

canonicalClaims.claim: KV cache OOM in long-context multi-tenant serving can be mitigated by (1) KV quantization to reduce per-token bytes, (2) admission control (max concurrent batch) to keep KV usage below capacity, and (3) prefix caching to share KV across requests with common prefixes.
conditions: PagedAttention or equivalent block-based KV management.
Workload has amenable structure (shared prefixes for (3)).
nonImplications: Does not imply mitigations preserve quality.
Does not imply admission control is always preferable to scaling out.

misconceptions.claim: Pipeline parallelism replicates KV cache across stages, giving more KV capacity per stage.
misconceptions.whyWrong: PP shards layers across stages; each stage holds only its layers' KV.

misconceptions.claim: Batch admission control has no effect on TTFT/TPOT stability.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Capping batch reduces preemption and stabilizes tail latency.

misconceptions.claim: KV quantization is always safe accuracy-wise.
misconceptions.whyWrong: INT4/FP8 KV can degrade quality on some tasks; INT8 is typically safer.

implementationFacts: vLLM supports INT8/FP8 KV cache via configuration.
Prefix caching is off by default in some versions; must be explicitly enabled.
performanceScenarios: Shared system prompts (agent workflows, tool-use) show 5-10x KV amortization with prefix caching.
